newsitem.title: UK: CE ups Northern Electric stake to 29.45 pct.
newsitem.headline: CE ups Northern Electric stake to 29.45 pct.

text.p: CE Electric UK Plc, the CalEnergy Co Inc unit bidding for Northern Electric Plc, raised its stake in the British utility to 29.45 percent on Friday, according to a stock market disclosure statement.
CE bought 2.7 million shares of Northern Electric at 630p per share, broker Hoare Govett said in the statement.
Northern Electric's shares continued their slump in early trade, dropping 18.5p to 605 on heavy volume, as rival "white knight" bidders failed to emerge and counter CE's hostile bid.
Northern Electric rejected CE's estimated 650 million stg bid last week, arguing it undervalued the company.
Analysts expect the regional electricity supplier will report glowing half-year results soon which would support its case that CE's bid was too low.
CE Electric is 70 percent owned by Nebraska-based CalEnergy, with the rest held by U.S. construction-to-telecoms group Peter Kiewit Sons.
